steps.text: Preheat the oven to 500 degrees F (260 degrees C).
Arrange peanuts in a single layer on a cookie sheet, and place in the preheated oven.
Turn the oven off. Leave peanuts in the oven for 1 hour without opening the door. Serve warm or at room temperature.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Peanuts
raw_recipe.description: Peanuts are so easy to roast at home. This recipe only requires raw peanuts, a hot oven, and the patience to keep the oven door closed for one whole hour — no matter how wonderful the peanut aroma!
raw_recipe.name: Roasted Peanuts

review.reviewBody: Love roasted peanuts. Make sure you read the directions, the oven is turned off while the peanuts are in it. Came out perfect!

Followed instructions EXACTLY!! Even though the shells looked OK the peanuts inside were burnt and inedible. Do not use this method. I have previously used other methods involving a lower temperature with the oven on and shaking the tray from time to time and that works just fine. Out now to buy more peanuts!

I'm almost 70 years young. I've been cooking for over 60 years. Yes, I began learning to cook at about the age of 8 years old. I live in Georgia, USA. I have grown peanuts for most of my life. I think I know just a wee bit about both cooking and about peanuts.

1. All ovens do NOT reach the same temperature according to the indicator, be it digital or manual. USE a "calibrated"
oven thermometer to be sure of the correct temperature.
2. There are numerous varieties of peanuts which vary in size. They also vary in the amount of "dryness" with which you are beginning.
3. Read the directions for the recipes THREE times before you begin to cook ANYTHING.
4. Follow the directions before you even consider changing the recipe.

Just a few words from the ancient cook.

As an engineer, looking at the distinct 2-party comments here, clearly something is being missed by some. 1. Are the peanuts different? (some raw but dry, others fresh, tiny or jumbo size? Have the husks been removed first?) The images show big one's husk on. 2. Everyone working in Fahrenheit, right? 3. Not all ovens cool at the same rate. The design of most is simple; "Get hot fast and don't burn down the kitchen!" I would not expect more than a 10% difference in cooling time between the ends of the spectrum though. However, big heavy pro-kitchen ovens cool slower than smaller ovens, and the dynamics is out the window if one has a "microwave/electric/countertop oven." 3. Human error. Like using three twice. Can happen to anyone!

Well I'm 70 and know nothing about cooking or peanuts. I followed the instructions with one other step, I washed the peanuts and patted dry before sprinkling the salt on. The peanuts tasted very good. I should have either cooked them a little less or used the full amount then the y may have been perfect.

Tried the recipe exactly, but the peanuts weren't roasted to the degree we like in our family. Left them in the oven after one hour, then turned the oven to 350 and roasted another 10 minutes. Perfect for us. I must say, the nuts I was roasting are large nuts, and may have actually needed more time in the beginning roast. Next time I'll try the original recipe, but leave them in for about 5 minutes before turning the oven off. Easy peasy!

My mom used this recipe plenty of times and it was great, but not reliable. Some would be overcooked if not stirred. The quickest method I have found is to microwave them for about 3-4 minutes in the microwave, then let them cool. They get crunchier as they cool. I do about 3 cups at a time in a microwaveable safe bowl.
This works better if you put the peanuts in the oven, then turn it on. Just be sure to turn the oven off when it reaches 500 degrees, then leave them for an hour.

This is the best, 'no fail' recipe I've ever tried. I've shared it with many, many others and have never
heard anything but raving, positive reviews. Thanks so much!!!! (Just remember - PREHEAT first - TURN OVEN OFF next - ADD PEANUTS (I check them in 45 mins, and sometimes take them out in about 50 mins. for me - if my husband is home I may cook the full hour for him.) Thanks for sharing - this recipe is BEYOND EASY.

Trick here is to know when your oven is adequately "pre-heated"....which is difficult with my oven. However, following the directions, the peanuts were no longer raw at the end of the hour, but I probably could have left them in another five or so minutes--or preheated my oven longer. Very simple recipe which works.
The temperature is too high. 400 degrees is far better than 500.

These were amazing! I was worried bc I have a new oven that cools down very quickly using a fan, but the peanuts turned out beautifully. The key is pay attention to the directions! Turn off the 500 degree oven right as you put the peanuts in, and leave them for an hour. Thank you for the recipe!

Anyone having a problem couldn’t have followed this great recipe. Either they forgot to turn oven off before putting peanuts in, or they didn’t start wim RAW peanuts, or opened oven when they shouldn’t have
Start with RAW or Green? it makes a difference !! The creator should say.
Couldn’t be easier! Turned out perfectly. I noticed it seems as if some forgot to turn off the oven before they put the peanuts in.

I’m 74 years old and have eaten parched peanuts my whole life. Used to see my Daddy sitting in front of the oven and testing them. This is PERFECT! They came just the way the peanuts are delicious, not too done but nice and just done. I have no idea how the lady’s nuts were burned. Mine are perfect. How easy is this! Thank you!

Easy, Perfect Results! What more can I say.. Follow instructions and you can't fail. Not to mention delish! If you burn em ya did something wrong. You can't burn peanuts in a preheated oven turned OFF
Thanks Kehn
I tried twice, both times they didn't cook. It was disappointing to say the least .
Despite resisting temptation to check after 30+ minutes when it started smelling good, I resisted. Opened door when alarm went off after an hour and had a tray of black burned nuts.

This is a great recipe. We preheat the oven to 500° place the peanuts in the oven and turn the oven off. We leave them in the oven for 1 hour and they are perfect. That's how we interpreted the recipe. Delicious. Best tasting peanuts we've had. Yummm
